blocks.heading: Explore the engine
blocks.html:
Learn your way around the GDevelop editor: the scene, the properties panel, the instance list, layers and image smoothing. You will fix a small soul-collecting game that has a few problems.

  • Change an object using only the Properties panel
  • Unlock and resize an object with the Instances list
  • Add a UI layer so the health bar stays on screen
  • Turn off image smoothing so pixel art looks sharp

blocks.heading: Get the project files
blocks.html:
⬇ DOWNLOAD the Chapter 1 project (zip)

  1. Save the zip, then right-click it and choose Extract All.
  2. Open the GDevelop app on your computer.
  3. Choose Open a project and pick lesson_1_game.json from the extracted folder.

You do not need a GDevelop account. Keep the assets folder next to the project file.

blocks.title: Task 1: Manipulate an object with the Properties panel
blocks.intro: Using only the Properties panel, make the large Ghost match the size, angle and position of the transparent LockedGhost.
steps: Click the large Ghost in the scene.
Open the Properties panel and change its position, size and angle.
Remember: the angle is 0 when the object faces right, and a smaller Y value moves an object up.
Check: the Ghost sits at X 640, Y 385, width 88, height 60, angle 0, exactly on top of the LockedGhost.

reveal.alt: The Properties panel for the Ghost with X 640, Y 385, W 88, H 60 and rotation 0 highlighted, next to the Ghost in the scene.

demo.alt: Animation: the large tilted Ghost is resized, rotated and moved until it sits exactly on top of the small transparent LockedGhost.
demo.caption: This is what you are aiming for: the big Ghost ends up exactly on top of the small one.

blocks.title: Task 2: Unlock an object with the Instances list
blocks.intro: The Background is locked, so you cannot select it in the scene.
steps: Open the Instances list panel.
Click the lock next to Background to unlock it.
Resize it to fill the whole game window (the black outline). You can lock it again afterwards.
Check: the Background fills the black game-window outline with no gaps.

reveal.alt: The Instances List panel open at the bottom of the editor with the Instances List button highlighted at the top right and the Background lock icon highlighted, showing how to unlock the Background.

blocks.title: Task 3: Add a UI layer with the Layers panel
blocks.intro: Right now the ResourceBar scrolls away with the game world. A UI layer keeps it fixed on the screen.
steps: Preview the game and move the Ghost down. Notice the bar does not stay put.
In the Layers panel, add a new layer and name it UI.
Select the ResourceBar and set its layer to UI in the Properties panel.
Preview again. Layers higher in the list appear on top.
Check: the ResourceBar stays at the bottom of the screen when the Ghost moves.

reveal.alt: The Layers panel with a new layer named UI and the Add a layer button highlighted, and the ResourceBar selected with its layer set to UI in the Properties panel.

blocks.title: Task 4: Change smoothing settings in the Resources tab
blocks.intro: One frame of the Ghost's idle animation looks blurry because of image smoothing.
steps: Preview the Ghost's idle animation and spot the blurry second frame.

Open the Project Manager: click the three-line menu button at the very top left of the window (on older versions it is a separate icon next to the clock and save icons). Go to Resources and select that image. Turn off Smooth the image.
To fix it for the whole game, open the Project Manager again, choose Properties under Game settings and change Scale mode from Linear to Nearest.
Check: the idle frames look sharp. Linear smoothing suits high-resolution art; Nearest (no smoothing) suits pixel art.

reveal.alt: The Project Manager opened with the three-line menu button at the top left highlighted, and Resources under Game settings highlighted.

more.alt: The Resources tab with the Ghost_Idle_2 image highlighted in the list and the Smooth the image box ticked.
Ghost_Idle_2.png selected with the Smooth the image box unticked.
Before and after: the blurry smoothed Ghost on the left and the sharp Ghost with smoothing turned off on the right.
